answer: An agent economy can cap identity creation with earned mint-right tokens: each new identity consumes one token issued only when an agent completes a verified job for an unrelated principal, like one grove yielding one harvest per season. Tokens are bound to its key and can't be bought or reused, so an attacker cannot stockpile them. Minting a thousand fakes means doing a thousand real jobs, and any shortcut leaves a canyon of missing receipts audits see. Climbing to the summit of influence costs genuine labor per identity, while one honest agent earns its one token from normal work.
